Subject: Hosted API commit tiers & pilot credits — initial proposal

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great conversation. Per your ask, I put together a concise proposal for a usage-based commit structure plus a pilot credit package so your engineers can validate latency and quality with real traffic. High level:

- Pilot: 250k free tokens (hosted API) for a 30-day POC, includes access to Redwood support channel and a dedicated onboarding session with a solutions engineer.
- Commit tiers (monthly equivalent):
  - Bronze: 1M tokens/month — list price (no commit discount).
  - Silver: 5M tokens/month — 15% off per-token.
  - Gold: 20M tokens/month — 28% off per-token + prioritized onboarding.
- Minimum commit term for Silver/Gold discounts: 3 months.
- Optional add-on: pilot SLA / extra monitoring (fee-based) — we can include a 60-day trial of Redwood Console Pro for the pilot.

Attached is a short term-sheet draft and an SLA summary for the pilot. If you can share a rough monthly token estimate for the first 3 months I can lock precise numbers and produce a formal quote.

Are you available for a 30-min call Wednesday to walk through details?

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tiers & pilot credits — initial proposal

Ben —

Thanks for the proposal. A few clarifying Qs from our side:

1) Can the pilot credits be applied to production usage if we convert mid-pilot, or are they strictly for POC traffic?
2) For the 15%/28% figures — are those off list per-token rates or off our current committed price? Please include example math (USD per 1k tokens) at each tier.
3) Procurement will want the minimum term length and an outline of what constitutes usage (prompt + generated tokens). Do you have a sample contract or MSA?

Estimated initial usage (week 1 of POC): ~400k tokens/week (spikes for batch rerankings). If pilot looks good we anticipate ramp to ~3–4M tokens/month within 2 months.

Can you also confirm if there are any constraints on KV cache persistence for hosted customers (we run long context conversations and want to avoid repeated prefix token costs).

Appreciate it — can do Wed 11am PT for a call.

—Stephanie
Head of Product, Acme AI
stephanie@acme.ai

Stephanie,

Great questions — answers inline and I added concrete per-1k token math for clarity:

1) Pilot credits: they are redeemable against hosted API usage and can be converted to production usage if you sign a commit during the pilot. If you convert mid-pilot we’ll pro-rate remaining credits and apply them to first invoice.

2) Discount basis: discounts are off our published hosted API per-token rates. Example (illustrative):
  - List: $0.006 / 1k tokens
  - Silver (5M/mo / 15%): $0.0051 / 1k tokens
  - Gold (20M/mo / 28%): $0.00432 / 1k tokens

3) Contract: attached term sheet is a one-page commercial summary. We typically follow with a standard MSA + SOW for pilots. Minimum commit term for the discounts above is 3 months; we can discuss longer terms for additional concessions.

KV cache: hosted customers get a session-level KV cache with best-effort persistence across requests; for strict persistence we recommend Dedicated or Private. We can run a short benchmark during the pilot to measure effective token savings.

Per your estimate (ramp to 3–4M/mo), Silver would be a good starting point. I’m attaching the term sheet again (RDW-Acme-Term-Sheet-v1.pdf) and a short pilot SLA spreadsheet.

Confirming Wed 11am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Ben

Attachments: RDW-Acme-Term-Sheet-v1.pdf, pilot-sla-summary.xlsx

Looping you in on Acme — they look promising and asked for a 250k pilot credit + potential conversion to 5M/mo (Silver) within 60 days. Two asks from sales:

- Approve an extra onboarding promo: +100k free tokens (so total 350k pilot) to reduce friction for their reranking tests.
- Approve up to 20% discount (vs published list) on Silver for an initial 3-month commit if they sign within the pilot window. Currently pricing shows 15% for Silver; sales requests discretionary 5% bridge to 20% for this net-new account.

I ran a quick cost model — additional 100k tokens in pilot is immaterial to economics and improves conversion probability. If we do 20% for the first 3 months we still preserve favorable unit economics given their expected growth.

Ben — can you confirm the ask on DocuSign timing and whether procurement will require additional security language?

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer
